learningObjective: Compute the effective cache-line utilization of a strided CPU access pattern and connect it to the arithmetic intensity seen by the memory system.

hardwareContext.architecture: modern x86-64 with 64 B cache lines

stem: A CPU loop reads a[i * S] for i = 0 .. N−1 where a is a contiguous FP32 array and S = 16 (stride 16 elements = 64 B). Cache lines are 64 B. Assuming N is large so warm-up effects are negligible and no prefetch reuse across iterations, what fraction of each transferred cache line is useful to the loop?

options.text: 1/16 (~6.25%): each 64 B cache line delivers only the 4 B accessed element; the remaining 60 B are transferred but unused.
1: hardware prefetchers combine adjacent strided loads into a single wide access, so effective utilization approaches 100% once the prefetcher locks on.
1/4: 4 B out of 16 B per element, computed against the SIMD lane width rather than the cache line width.
1/2: modern out-of-order cores double the effective utilization by reading two elements per cache line through speculative execution.

explanation: Stride 16 × 4 B = 64 B means each iteration accesses one FP32 element that lives in a different 64 B cache line. Each line delivers 64 B; only 4 B are used. Utilization = 4 / 64 = 1/16 ≈ 6.25%. Hardware prefetchers may still fetch the correct next line, but they do not reduce per-line waste; speculative execution and SIMD width also do not change bytes moved per line.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: only 4 B out of every 64 B cache line are consumed.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: prefetching improves latency hiding, not per-line utilization; wasted bytes still traverse the memory system.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: SIMD lane width does not divide cache line bytes into 'useful vs wasted'; the cache line is the transfer granularity.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: out-of-order execution reorders memory ops but does not deliver more of a cache line as useful.

assumptions: Each accessed element lies in a distinct 64 B cache line (stride 16 × 4 B = 64 B).
No temporal reuse within the loop; each iteration touches a fresh line.
Cache pressure is high enough that prefetched but unused bytes cannot be later re-used.
nonImplications: Does not imply reordering the loop cannot help; a stride-1 access pattern would achieve 100% utilization.
Does not imply hardware prefetchers are useless; they still reduce miss latency even when per-line waste is high.

distractorRationales.B: Confuses latency hiding with bandwidth utilization.
distractorRationales.C: Applies SIMD arithmetic to a cache-line question.

sourceRefs.locator: Memory hierarchy chapter; cache-line utilization and spatial locality

performanceClaim.scope: generic x86-64 CPU, 64 B cache lines, stride-16 FP32 access
